notes.meaning: A father warns his son against promising to pay someone else's debt without thinking it through. Shaking hands on such an agreement traps a person with his own spoken words. It is foolish to risk your family's safety on a loan you might not be able to afford.

Anyone who has made a reckless promise like this must act right away to get free. Swallow your pride, go straight to the other person, and plead earnestly until the debt matter is settled. Do not even take a nap until you have escaped the danger, just like a wild deer or bird fleeing a hunter's trap.

Lazy people are told to look at the tiny ant and learn good sense. Even though the ant has no boss, officer, or king telling it what to do, it works hard on its own. It gathers food during the harvest so it has plenty to eat when hard times come.

The teacher challenges the lazy person who keeps lying in bed instead of doing his duty. The slacker constantly begs for just a little more sleep and a little more rest. Because of this habit, poverty will sneak up on him like a bandit and take everything with overwhelming force.

A corrupt and worthless person uses dishonest speech wherever he goes. He hides his real motives by winking his eyes, shuffling his feet, and signaling with his fingers. He uses secret gestures to plot trouble while trying to avoid being caught.

This troublemaker has a twisted heart and continually stirs up fights between people. Because he spends his life planning harm for others, ruin will strike him suddenly and without warning. He will be shattered like a clay pot, completely beyond recovery.

The Lord deeply hates certain evil behaviors, using a list of six and then seven to highlight the very worst sins. At the top of the list are proud eyes that look down on others, a tongue that tells lies, and hands that kill innocent people. Pride comes first because it is at the root of so many other sins.

The list continues with a heart that dreams up evil schemes and feet that rush eagerly toward doing wrong. God also detests a witness who lies under oath in court, and worst of all, someone who stirs up quarrels among family and friends. Sowing discord is especially hated because it destroys love and peace in a community.

A son is urged to hold onto the godly teachings and commands given by his father and mother. These lessons should never be discarded as one grows up, but kept close like a treasured necklace. Keeping God's truth bound to the heart protects a person's inner thoughts and desires.

God's truth will guide your steps while you walk, watch over you while you sleep, and fill your thoughts when you wake up. His command is like a lamp that shines light on a dark path, showing you how to live rightly. Accepting correction and discipline is the only true way to life.

Keeping God's word close protects a young person from an immoral woman. She uses sweet talk and flattering words to draw someone into sin while hiding the deadly trap. True wisdom sees through these smooth lies before any damage is done.

A person must not let sinful desire grow in his heart, nor get pulled in by an unfaithful woman's flirting glances. Visiting a prostitute can quickly cost a man all his wealth, leaving him with only a crust of bread. Even worse, committing adultery with another man's wife can cost him his very life.

No one can scoop fire into his lap without burning his clothes, or walk on hot coals without scorching his feet. In the exact same way, anyone who sleeps with another man's wife will face certain ruin. You cannot touch what belongs to someone else and expect to escape punishment.

People may feel some pity for a starving thief who steals food just to keep himself alive. Even so, if he gets caught, he must pay back many times what he took, even if it costs him all his belongings. Theft can at least be repaid with money, which sets up a contrast with far worse sins.

A man who commits adultery has no good sense at all, because he is actually destroying his own life. Unlike a hungry thief, he acts only out of selfish lust. He will suffer physical wounds, lasting disgrace, and a ruined reputation that can never be wiped away.

An injured husband will be filled with burning rage when he discovers the betrayal. When the day of vengeance arrives, he will show no mercy and refuse to hold back. No amount of money or expensive bribes will calm his anger or buy his forgiveness.
